study_identification_part.si_4_title: Normative modeling of brain MRI data identifies small subcortical volumes and associations with cognitive function in youth with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD)

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: CIFASD was used for the clinical evaluation of youth with FASD and a comparison group; ENIGMA datasets were the source of normative training data for the CentileBrain model used.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: Participants were children and adolescents, ages 8-17, who were part of a Collaborative Initiative on FASD (CIFASD) study ... notably, the training data used in creating the CentileBrain model were primarily collected from the Enhancing Neuroimaging Genetics through Meta-Analysis (ENIGMA) Consortium.

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: Using a sample of youth with FASD and typically-developing comparisons ... we calculated z-scores ... using CentileBrain (Ge et al., 2024) ... dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The CentileBrain normative model was built using 37,407 comparison brains.
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: Individual regional volumetric z-scores were generated using CentileBrain (Ge et al., 2024), an open source online software tool that leverages an aggregated neuroimaging dataset with a large number of individuals (37,407 comparison brains).
